target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Y P : Type) (N : S1 X Y) (v : P → N.D1 → N.D1) (T : ℕ),
    ∃ N' : S1 (X × P) Y, N'.D9 ∧ N'.d13 = T ∧
      ∀ xs : List (X × P), xs.length ≤ T → N'.d4 xs = N.d16 v xs
a_raw: {"translation": "Target defines (names, without proving) the following proposition: For all types X, Y, and P; every finite-node transition system N with input type X and output type Y (consisting of a finite type of nodes, a state type and an initial state for each node, a per-node update function taking a global state—an assignment of a state to every node—and an input in X to a new state for that node, and an output function from global states to Y); every function v assigning to each p in P a transformation from global states of N to global states of N; and every natural number T; there exists a finite-node transition system N' with input type X × P and output type Y (with its own finite type of nodes, per-node state types, initial states, per-node update functions, and output function, all of which may depend on X, Y, P, N, v, and T) such that all three of the following hold: (1) Acyclicity of dependencies: defining a directed edge from node m to node n in N' to hold whenever there exist two global states σ, σ' of N' that agree on every node other than m and an input (x, p) in X × P such that n's update function produces different values on (σ, (x, p)) and (σ', (x, p)), there is no node n of N' with a non-empty directed path (of length at least 1) from n to n along this edge relation—so N' has neither self-dependencies nor longer directed cycles. (2) Exact node count: the number of nodes of N' is equal to T (literally T, not merely at most T and independent of the number of nodes of N). (3) Output agreement on inputs of length at most T: for every finite sequence xs of pairs (x, p) in X × P with length at most T, the output of N' on xs equals the output of N on xs under v. Here, the output of N' on xs is obtained by starting from N''s initial global state, synchronously updating all nodes of N' for each pair (x, p) in xs from left to right, and applying N''s output function to the final global state; while the output of N on xs under v is obtained by starting from N's initial global state, processing each pair (x, p) in xs from left to right by first taking one synchronous update step of N on input x and then applying v(p) to the resulting global state, and finally applying N's output function to the resulting global state. Nothing is required about the behavior of N' on sequences of length strictly greater than T, no restrictions are placed on X, Y, P, or v, and no restrictions (such as finiteness or any relation to N's state types) are placed on the per-node state types of N'."}

divergences.description: In the formal model S1, systems are restricted to discrete-time, deterministic, finite-unit machines, while per-unit state types (A3) and update/readout functions (a5, a6) are completely unconstrained. Target imposes no restriction relating N''s unit state types to N's or limiting computation in a6, and D9 requires only acyclicity of unit-to-unit dependencies in a5 (allowing all units to read the current input directly and a6 to read all units); this idealization is what allows an exact T-unit feedforward system regardless of the number of units in N.

The formal definition S1.d16 fixes a specific operational timing for interventions that the description leaves implicit: for each pair (x, p) in the sequence, N first performs one synchronous update step d2 on x and then applies v p to the resulting global state, with no intervention applied on the empty sequence.

Regarding Usher's passage [P-U], the description accurately quotes 'reactions to structural perturbations' and cautiously hedges what it may mean, but it is worth noting that v : P → N.D1 → N.D1 models state transformations rather than structural perturbations (such as altering units, connectivity, or update functions) even for the original system N.

judgement.summary: Target faithfully formalizes the author's description—matching all quantifiers, the loop-free condition, the exact T-unit count, and output agreement on sequences of length at most T—and the description accurately reports both Doerig et al. and Usher without overclaiming. Only minor modeling idealizations (unconstrained unit state types and readout in S1, and the specific post-update timing of interventions in S1.d16) are left implicit.
